text: dsh-model-pin（DSH 插件）：按 provider 限制模型请求。它在 agent/request 阶段检查模型，允许列表内的请求原样通过；未允许的模型可重定向到 fallback，或由 reject 模式拒绝。插件还观察 llm/stream 中已配置 provider 的模型切换并记录提示。适合希望固定本地模型或管理不同 provider 可用模型的 DSH 用户。需为 provider 配置非空 allow 列表；fallback 默认取列表首项，切换提示默认开启，不需额外 API key 或账号。

dsh-model-pin limits models per DSH provider. Allowed requests pass unchanged; other models are redirected to a fallback or rejected. It logs model changes during streaming. Configure a non-empty allow list; the fallback defaults to its first entry. No API key or account is needed.

Keep DSH requests on an explicit allow-list of models per provider.

dsh-model-pin 的功能「provider 模型允许列表」：配置非空 allow 列表后，已允许模型通过，其他模型可重定向或拒绝。由请求解析阶段自动触发。
dsh-model-pin 的功能「重定向或拒绝」：未允许的模型请求可改用 fallback，或以清晰错误拒绝。通过 provider 的 action 配置选择行为。
dsh-model-pin 的功能「模型切换提示」：观察已配置 provider 的模型流；模型变化时记录提示，供用户注意路由器重载。由 llm/stream 自动触发。
如何给每个 DSH 模型提供商设定可用模型范围？
Stop DSH from selecting models outside my configured provider list.

dsh-model-pin README · dsh-model-pin：A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin for machines that cannot afford model roulette: keep every model request inside an allowed set per provider, redirect the rest to a fallback (or refuse them), and get a warning whenever a request would make a llama.cpp router reload models.

dsh-model-pin README · The problem it fixes：dsh lets every chat pick its own model, and background helpers can request yet another one. On a machine that can only keep one local model loaded, each stray request either fails or evicts the loaded model: minutes of reloading, prompt cache gone (discussion #3199). Worse, subagents inherit the model their parent session was CREATED with, not the one it currently uses, so they quietly land on stale or wrong routes (#455, #1581).

dsh-model-pin README · The problem it fixes：dsh-model-pin enforces an allow-list at dsh's own resolution layer (the `agent/request` waterfall, whose documentation calls returning a replacement "the sanctioned switch path"). Every request from every session is resolved against the list at step boundaries: subagents, retries, and, once the pinned route is logged, session-title and compaction calls too. Persisted session data is never rewritten.

dsh-model-pin README · Install：```
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-model-pin
```

Then in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: model-pin
  config:
    providers:
      llamacpp:

Unconfigured providers are never touched.

dsh-model-pin README · What it looks like：```
model-pin: llamacpp session=059a680f turn 3 redirecting qwen3.8 -> qwen3.8-q4-long (not in allow)
model-pin: llamacpp model switch qwen3.8-q4-long -> qwen3.8-fast (a --models-max 1 router reloads now; the previous model's prompt cache is lost)
```

With `action: reject`, a disallowed request fails the turn with a clear message instead (`model-pin: model "x" is not in the allowed set for provider "llamacpp" (allowed: ...)`), and dsh's retry never loops on it.

dsh-model-pin README · What you should know：- The web model picker does not know about the pin: it may keep displaying the model you clicked while every request actually runs on the fallback. The redirect line in the terminal (or /logs, if dsh-logbook is installed) shows what actually ran.
- The pin has the last word over the picker because it registers at profile load, before any agent exists (first-registered waterfall listeners are outermost in cordis). Another root plugin loaded before this one could still override it.
- The switch warning is observation only; it cannot block a reload. Pair it with a one-entry allow-list if you want reloads gone entirely.
- Cross-provider redirection is out of scope for v1: requests for a provider you did not configure pass through, including a subagent stuck on a deleted provider.
- Related work: [dsh-model-switch](https://github.com/NOirBRight/dsh-model-switch) is the opposite personality: a polished per-role model router with web UI panels, deliberately without global enforcement. dsh-model-pin is config-first, headless-friendly, and about restriction, not routing.
